name: Hoenderpastei
summary: Chicken pie the old Cape way: chicken poached with allspice and cloves, set in a lemony sago-thickened sauce with sliced boiled egg, under golden puff pastry.
about: Hoenderpastei is an heirloom of Cape and Afrikaans cooking, going back to colonial-era recipes spiced with allspice, cloves and mace. The stock is thickened with sago and enriched with egg yolk and lemon, and slices of hard-boiled egg (sometimes ham) go into the filling. It is a Sunday and Christmas dish, served with yellow rice and vegetables.

ingredients.name: Dry white wine
ingredients.note: or extra stock with 1 tbsp more lemon juice

ingredients.name: Sago
ingredients.note: soaked in 0.5 cup water for 20 minutes

ingredients.name: Ground nutmeg
ingredients.note: or a pinch of ground mace

ingredients.name: Puff pastry
ingredients.note: 400 g roll, thawed in the fridge

steps: Put the chicken, water, onion, bay leaves, allspice, cloves, peppercorns, stock cube and salt in a large pot. Bring to the boil over high heat, skim off any foam, then cover and simmer over low heat for 1 hour, until the meat falls easily off the bones.

Lift out the chicken and let it cool for 10 minutes. Strain the stock and measure it: you need 3 cups, so boil it down or top it up with water. Pull the meat into bite-sized pieces and discard the skin, bones and whole spices.

Return the 3 cups of stock to the pot with the wine and bring to the boil. Stir in the soaked sago and simmer over medium-low heat, stirring often, for 10–12 minutes until the grains are clear and the sauce has thickened. Stir in the butter and nutmeg.

Beat the egg yolk with the lemon juice in a bowl. Whisk in a ladle of the hot sauce, then stir the mixture back into the pot off the heat; do not let it boil again or the yolk will curdle. Fold in the chicken and ham, taste for salt, and leave to cool for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Spoon half the filling into a deep 25 cm pie dish, lay the egg slices over it, then cover with the rest of the filling.

Unroll the pastry and lay it over the dish, trimming it to overhang by 1 cm. Press the edge onto the rim, crimp with a fork, cut two small slits in the centre for steam and brush all over with beaten egg.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until the pastry is puffed and deep golden and the filling bubbles at the slits. Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with yellow rice and green beans or pumpkin.
prepNote: Make the filling a day ahead and refrigerate; top with pastry and bake straight from the fridge, adding 10 minutes.
